extracted.intended_audience: rural householders, farmers, sanitary engineers, and local public-health workers
extracted.subtask_description: An early-20th-century engineering-oriented manual on rural public health and sanitation, covering measurement of community health, site selection, house and barn construction, water and sewage systems, food and milk safety, prevention and control of infectious diseases, and legal/regulatory aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vital statistics of rural life
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of death-rate and other population statistics to measure community health and compare rural and urban conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the general death-rate (deaths per 1000 population) and discusses its limitations (averaging, effects of age/sex/nationality/occupation, record accuracy). Includes subtopics: death-rates (ideal and by district), accuracy of records, effect of children on death-rate, death-rates of children, typhoid fever statistics, typhoid in small cities, seasonal and demographic influences. Emphasizes careful interpretation of statistics (e.g., underreporting in rural areas, composition effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of a house -- soil and surroundings
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for siting houses with respect to soils, drainage, topography, and nearby vegetation to promote healthfulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists considerations: damp soils, proper house location, objections to trees near houses, spacing between houses, composition of soils, links between soil conditions and disease (e.g., cancer cited), topography, effects of cultivation, made ground, presence of water in soil, drainage, and ground-water considerations. Implies grading and drainage design to turn surface water away from dwellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of houses and barns with reference to healthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural and construction methods for dwellings and farm buildings that reduce dampness, soil air infiltration, and improve sanitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers shutting out soil air, position of drain outfalls, cellar dampness, use of tar or asphalt, dry masonry for cellar walls, damp courses, cellar floors, cellar ventilation, privy design, cow-stable construction, and use of concrete. Emphasizes practical selection of methods and need for details tailored by householder or engineer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ventilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practical measures for providing adequate ventilation in dwellings and farm buildings to avoid polluted air and its health effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses effects of bad air, modifying circumstances, dangers of polluted air, effects of changes in air, air composition and organic matter, design and placement of fresh-air inlets and foul-air outlets, sizing openings, ventilation of stables, costs, and relation of heating to ventilation. Includes examples and devices (figures referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity of water required for domestic use
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimating domestic and farm water needs and design guidance for storage to meet demand and fire requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses modern tendencies, per-person water requirements, water used in stables, maximum consumption rates and variations, fire-stream requirements, rain-water supply calculations, storage computations for rain collection and brook-fed reservoirs, and potential deficiencies from well supplies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of water-supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of possible water sources (wells, springs, brooks, ponds) and guidance for protecting and developing them for household use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers underground waters, ordinary dug wells and their construction, deep wells, springs and extensions, brook supplies, storage reservoirs, ponds/lakes, and pressure/head considerations. Includes diagrams for springs and well sinking and emphasizes protection from contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of water
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and indicators of water quality, addressing mineral and biological contamination and implications for domestic use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats mineral matter and its effects (e.g., loss of soap), vegetable and animal pollution, hazards of polluted well water, and danger assessment. Implies need for water protection and treatment where contaminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water-works construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and construction principles for collecting, storing, pumping and distributing rural water supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes methods of collection, spring reservoirs, stream supplies, dams, waste weirs, gate houses, pipe lines, pumping options (windmills, hydraulic rams, hot-air engines, gas engines, steam pumps, air lifts), tanks, and pressure tanks. Contains practical installations and figures illustrating equipment and arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plumbing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for household plumbing installation, hot-water systems, sinks, laundry tubs, and house drainage to ensure sanitary conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses installation practices, supply tanks, main supply piping, hot-water circulation, kitchen sinks, laundry tubs, hot-water boilers, attachments to stoves, fixtures (wash-basins, baths), cost considerations, house drainage, trap-vents, and types of water-closets (washout, washdown, syphonic, syphon-jet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sewage disposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Options and design principles for disposal and treatment of household sewage to prevent pollution and disease spread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines sewage, discusses stream pollution, treatment on land (surface application), artificial sewage beds, subsurface tile disposal, automatic syphon, sedimentation, and underdrains. Includes septic tank plans and guidance for single-house disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and care of milk and meat
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices to reduce bacterial contamination of milk and dangers of diseased meat; slaughterhouse considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers bacteria in milk, effects of bacterial contamination, diseases transmitted by milk, methods for obtaining clean milk, city milk hazards, and dangers associated with diseased meat and slaughter-house practices. Emphasizes cleanliness from production through handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foods and beverages
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines on human nutrition, balanced rations, cooking, appetite, and the health effects of drinks, condiments, tobacco, and drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses digestive processes, teachings of digestion, balanced rations, individual habit effects, cooking, muscular and psychic reactions, water consumption, condiments and drinks, tobacco, and the drug habit. Implies dietary recommendations and behavior modification for health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual-level practices for maintaining health: exercise, clothing, bathing, breathing, eyesight, teeth, and sleep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses exercise, appropriate clothing, bathing practices, dangers of mouth-breathing, eye care, dental health, and sleep hygiene. Provides practical recommendations for daily habits to promote individual health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theories of disease
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of causation and susceptibility factors for disease (dirt, resistance, heredity, parasites, bacteria, toxins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines effects of dirt, blood resistance, cell disintegration, heredity, age and sex, occupation, direct causes of disease, parasites, bacterial agencies, antitoxins, natural immunity, chemical poisons, and external causes. Context for preventive measures and public-health practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and methods for disinfecting premises, objects, and persons using chemical and physical agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes disinfecting agents, antiseptics, deodorizers, patented disinfectants, disinfecting gases (sulfur, formaldehyde), liquid disinfectants (carbolic acid, coal-tar products, mercury, lime, soap), and methods using heat (dry heat, boiling water, steam), drying, light, and soil exposure. Includes practical procedures for quarantine and cleaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuberculosis and pneumonia
rubrics_metrics.description: Preventive guidance and individual/community measures for tuberculosis (consumption) and pneumonia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses tuberculosis and individual resistance, precautions by consumptives, prospects for cure, pneumonia as a germ disease (weather not primary cause), preventives for pneumonia, and infection mechanisms. Includes recommendations like outdoor sleeping porches for consumptives (figures referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typhoid fever
rubrics_metrics.description: Causes, transmission routes, and control measures for typhoid fever with specific well- and milk-protection guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the bacillus, transmission methods, well-construction to prevent typhoid, milk infection routes (including flies), other sources of infection, and treatment approaches. Emphasizes water-supply protection and public-health actions to reduce typhoid incidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition, contagion characteristics, and quarantine/precautionary measures for common childhood infectious diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses after-effects, preliminary symptoms, contagiousness, quarantine recommendations for scarlet fever, characteristics of measles eruptions, whooping cough precautions, and chickenpox. Emphasizes parental responsibility (mother keeping sick children at home) and isolation to prevent spread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parasitical diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and control strategies for vector-borne and parasitic diseases such as malaria, yellow fever, hookworm, pellagra, and plague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers malaria and mosquito transmission, elimination and limitation of mosquito infection, yellow fever characteristics, hookworm disease, pellagra, and bubonic plague. Emphasizes vector control (mosquito elimination) and public-health measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diseases controlled by antitoxins
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of vaccine/antitoxin use and protocols for diseases like smallpox, diphtheria, rabies, and tetanus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses smallpox (value of vaccination, characteristics, treatment), diphtheria (cause, antitoxin production, symptoms), rabies, and tetanus. Emphasizes value and methods of vaccination/antitoxin treatments and public-health implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hygiene and law
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and regulatory principles underpinning public-health laws: basis, enforcement, and specific regulatory areas (water, food, milk, quarantine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses principles of hygiene law, self-interest as a basis for law, quality-of-water regulations, food regulations and pure-food laws, protection of milk, and quarantine laws. Emphasizes relationship between legal authority and community protection; illustrates how law complements sanitary practice.
